newsitem.title: INDIA: India Gandhi bride weds in privacy amid security.
newsitem.headline: India Gandhi bride weds in privacy amid security.

text.p: Priyanka Gandhi, daughter of assassinated prime minister Rajiv Gandhi and heiress of Indias leading political family, was married on Tuesday in a zealously private ceremony held amid tight security.

"Priyanka Gandhi and Robert Vadra were married this evening in a traditional Hindu wedding ceremony," her family said in a statement in New Delhi. "The two hour-long ceremony was conducted according to Kashmiri Pandit rites."
Priyanka, 25, and her 27-year-old husband, an exporter, posed for photographers after the ceremony held at the residence of Sonia Gandhi, Rajivs Italian-born widow.

Indias "royal wedding," as some called it, raised questions after media reports that the government, bound by law to provide top-grade security to the family, was planning to allot the newly weds a sprawling bungalow in the heart of the capital.
The Press Trust of India reported that a court in the central state of Madhya Pradesh on Tuesday admitted a public interest petition against the move to allot such a house.

Rajiv, his mother Indira Gandhi, and her father Jawaharlal Nehru, were all Indian prime ministers. Rajiv and Indira, who faced separatist threats, were both assassinated. Priyanka is not a public figure.
President Shankar Dayal Sharma, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Vice-President K.R. Narayanan were among the wedding guests, most of whom were family friends.
Domestic newspapers reported that Sonia wrote a carefully-worded letter to scores of friends seeking their blessings for the couple, but gently pointing to a decision to keep the wedding private.

"These (wedding) rites were the same as those which solemnised the marriage of Indira and Feroze Gandhi in 1942. For the wedding, the bride wore a South Indian temple sari which had belonged to her grandmother, Indira Gandhi," the statement said.
One hundred policemen stood on watch outside the single-storeyed bungalow located near a sprawling lawn and guarded by crack commandos.

Inside, the bride and groom arrived with Sonia Gandhi and Priyankas brother, Rahul, and briefly posed for photos amid glowing earthen lamps and decorative flower garlands in the house, which was illuminated on all sides by electric lights.

Vadra, described in the Indian media as a well-behaved man who enjoys disco dancing, wore a cream-coloured closed-neck jacket, trousers and a turban, while Priyanka sported a red sari with golden brocades, draped over her head in Hindu style.
Sitaram Kesri, the president of Indias Congress party, was among the guests.
Sonia wields considerable influence on the party, which has ruled India for all but four years since independence in 1947, although she has shown no interest in politics.

Her husband, Rajiv, was assassinated by a female Tamil suicide bomber in 1991 in what is believed to be a revenge killing for his decision to send Indian troops to disarm Sri Lankan Tamil separatists in 1987.

A hoarding put up by Congress workers outside Sonia Gandhis residence, which is next to the Congress headquarters, displayed her portrait and urged her help in uniting the fractious party, which was routed in general elections last year.
"To keep the great traditions of the country, a humble appeal to Mrs. Sonia Gandhi: Congresss unity is the countrys unity," it said.
